_about: Named viewer settings (not to be confused with the repo root's capture_presets.json, which holds capture settings for the Python pipeline). Each key is a panel control's id and the value it is set to, exactly as if the slider had been moved by hand. 'reliefscale': 'grid' means match the grid size. Keys about the preset itself: 'short' is the button's text and 'label' its tooltip; 'view' presses a camera button; 'camera' frames a shot (azimuth and elevation in degrees, distance in tiles); 'research' shows the button only in Research mode; 'chapter' makes it a story step instead of a button, with 'caption' shown over the canvas ({tiles}, {size}, {world}, {scene}, {source}, {collects}, {exposed} are filled in from the tileset). Add your own; the viewer lists whatever is here.

heights.label: Material by altitude alone, no region filter.

plain.label: The capture alone: no terrain, no rule, no far field. For scenes that are not ground tiles.

proof-on.label: Rule on, flat light, survey view: the on/off figure.

ch1.label: Tiles of ground, close up, outlined.
ch1.caption: 1 · capture Each outlined square is one tile: {size} of {source}, rebuilt so that its four edges can meet other tiles. Everything that follows is built from {tiles} of these.

ch2.label: Wang tiles and their edge colours.
ch2.caption: 2 · tiles Wang tiles. Each edge carries a colour (the bands); a tile sits only next to tiles whose touching edge has the same colour, and the patch for that colour is centred on the edge, so the ground continues across it with no search. This part reimplements GSWT (Zeng, Ma and Sander, 2025).

ch3.label: The tiles laid over terrain, materials at random.
ch3.caption: 3 · world The same {tiles} tiles over generated, eroded terrain, {world} across, continued to the horizon by the far field. Each cell's material is chosen at random: the baseline.

ch4.label: The same world with materials placed by the land.
ch4.caption: 4 · rule Each material placed from the terrain: {collects} collects in hollows and channels, {exposed} stays on steep, convex ground. In Hybrid GSWT this coverage is painted by hand; here it is computed. Compare with step 3, or turn on show the decision under materials.
